meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (1MA1/1H, Thursday 16 May 2024, P76923A), downloaded from qualifications.pearson.com. Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Coded in the same sitting as EDEXCEL-JUN24-F-P1 so the crossover block carries identical tags. The shared block is 1F q20–q26 = 1H q1–q7, contiguous on both papers, and the marks match item for item (2, 3, 5, 3, 4, 4, 5). All 23 (Total for Question) lines recovered and summing to the printed 80. Coded WITH mark_split.

coding_notes: q1–q7 are 1F q20–q26 and carry identical skill tags, kinds and mark splits to that file, by design.

q11 (a translation followed by a rotation, described as one transformation) tagged rotations then translations: the single equivalent transformation is a rotation, and the translation is the step that fixes its centre.

q12 coded as three separate 1-mark rows, as the paper prints them. Each is tagged sketching_functions, following the OCR-JUN25-F-P1 q15 ruling that matching standard graph shapes to equations is that node rather than quadratic_functions — which would be a false claim for the cubic and the reciprocal anyway.

q21 (height of a cuboid from its volume and total surface area) tags areas_of_squares_and_rectangles for the surface area, the documented handling for the cuboid-surface-area gap, alongside volume_of_a_prism and the quadratic the elimination produces.

q16 tagged conditional_probability alone. The answer is an algebraic identity, but what it tests is that the second draw's denominator has fallen by one; algebraic_proof would credit a proof technique the item does not exercise.
q19 tagged congruence_and_similarity: both mark-scheme routes are a scale factor between the two similar triangles, one of them via a perpendicular height.
